name: Modular construction and industrialised building systems
principle: Modular construction moves fabrication from the congested site into controlled workshops: equipment, piping, cable and steel are assembled into transportable modules (skids, multi-storey modules, e-houses), shipped, lifted and connected on site. Benefits are schedule compression, quality, weather independence, lower site headcount and local content limits; the trade-offs are transport envelope limits, module weight for lifting, joint design at every module interface, and early engineering freeze. Industrialised Building Systems (IBS) applies the same offsite logic to buildings — precast components, panelised and volumetric systems — promoted in Malaysia through the CIDB IBS programme with content and scoring rules.

process_steps.name: Facility split into modules within transport and lift limits
Modules fabricated, piped, cabled and inspected in the yard
Modules transported by road, barge or vessel
Modules set, levelled and interconnects (piping, cable, tie-ins) completed

limitations: module interfaces concentrate risk: every split is a fabricated joint on site
early freeze conflicts with normal design iteration; the schedule benefit is lost if design is late
advantages: yard quality and productivity transfer to site as compressed schedule and lower headcount
e-houses and skids reduce hot work and congested-site labour exposure
